62 cm chain, enters through the top 6.3 cm from y=606 and stops at (24.0, 548.4, 53.6), 53.4 cm from the nearest face (z), 21.5 cm from the cathode and 177 cm from the APA seam, in APA1 (x>0, z<231). The hot 2.5 cm piece 97012 (1.1e5) is on the chain, cos_fwd -0.99: the Bragg peak itself, not a hot tip past the end. A 10 cm arm (97011 8.4 cm + 97001 1.7 cm, d 0-7.4, cos_fwd 0.43) leaves the stop at plateau charge (5.5-6.0e4), hooking off the muon line in all three azimuths; a muon at its Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, so this is the Michel. Four small pieces 17-41 cm out, all 16-35 cm to +x of the body line on the Michel side, stepping down in time in f_meas away from the Michel: 279007 and 280008 (along the Michel direction) and 282010 are gamma; 281009 is +35 cm in x like the Michel but -22 in z (cos_fwd -0.36), called gamma, arguable. No dead channels at the stop in f_meas.

201 cm single-segment chain, enters through the top 12.9 cm from y=606 and stops at (51.6, 408.8, 302.5), 160 cm from the nearest face, 49 cm from the cathode and 71.5 cm from the APA seam, in APA3. The profile rides a ragged 4-6e4 plateau (dip to 3.7e4 at s 31-35), bumps to ~9e4 at s 7-9 and climbs to ~1.2e5 (about 2x plateau) over the last 2-3 cm, on the muon curve; short but a real rise, and the last point sits at the peak, so no overshoot. A 10.8 cm arm 142003 (d 0-10.2, cos_fwd 0.81) leaves the stop at plateau charge (4-8.5e4, no climb at its far end): in f_meas the track reverses direction in time slice at the stop in U, V and W, and in the c azimuth the arm bends ~60 deg off the muon line. A muon at its Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, so the arm is the Michel; not a hot tip (10 cm at plateau, not a couple of cm at several times it). 348001 (2 points, 12.6-12.9 cm, cos_fwd 0.68) sits on the Michel line 2.5 cm past its end: tagged michel as the electron continuation across a small break; gamma would be the alternative. 350002 is a 2-point speck 54 cm back up the muon side, ~20 cm off the body line, opposite the Michel direction: delta / other. No dead channels at the stop in any plane (W dead bands are 100+ channels away).

The stop is 55 cm from the anode face, 96 from the seam, 135 from the front face, 220 below the top and 297 from the cathode. column21: 265 cm chain entering 0.3 cm from the z face and ending 132.4 cm from the nearest wall, deeply contained. This is the cleanest Bragg in my chunk: a 5.3e4 plateau beyond s=40 climbing smoothly along the solid muon curve through 6.0e4 at s=20, 6.7-7.5e4 at s=10-18, 8.7-9.0e4 at s=6-13, 9.5-1.02e5 at s=3-4, 1.14-1.22e5 at s=1.5-2.5 and 1.39e5 at s=0.5, with the row mean for the last segment 58015 quoted at 1.05e5 over its 7.8 cm. The rise is monotone over 20 cm and the peak is at the origin, so the pin does not move and no undershoot applies (nothing sits forward of the fit end at several times MIP). Past the stop there is exactly one thing: 222018, two points spanning 0.3 cm, 9.3 cm from the stop, 7.3 cm past it and 5.7 cm off the entry-stop chord, carrying 2.0e4 e/cm and 0.5 MeV, and the chain itself records that it was bridged to the stop vertex across 9.11 cm of EMPTY space rather than by a graph edge. f_meas confirms the gap: in all three planes the speck is a single isolated brown dot at time slice 1058 with a clean charge-free break below it before the track s own hits resume at 1040. That is the rubric s attachment tie-break in its literal form -- a 0.3 cm two-point speck across a 9 cm gap is not a 35 MeV electron -- so it is a detached dot, gamma, not a michel, and the verdict stays STM_ONLY. 220017 is the second dot, two points over 4.5 cm, 41.6 cm out, 17.6 cm past the stop and 37.6 cm off the chord; I measured it at 42 degrees from 222018 as seen from the stop, i.e. on the same side of the stop as the decay charge rather than scattered in an unrelated direction, and charge is explicitly not a criterion for a faint speck at 40 cm, so gamma as well. 58010 is the one thing close and backward: 10 points over 5.5 cm, 4.0 cm back along the muon, 3.3 cm off the chord at cos_fwd -0.87, and the chain body-excludes it as pdg 11 -- that is the delta / other rule almost word for word. Two gammas and no michel gives detached dots.

85.8 cm chain in one fitted segment (52003, 145 pts, mean 56941). It enters exactly at the anode x face (d_face 0.0) and stops 37.0 cm from the z wall, 68 cm from the anode, in_fv 1. The Bragg is the cleanest in my chunk: the profile sits on a 4.5-6.5e4 band out beyond s = 20 and then tracks the muon reference curve point for point over the last 15 cm - 6.5e4 at s = 13, 8.0e4 at s = 8, 9.0e4 at s = 5, 1.00e5, 1.12e5, 1.18e5 and 1.23e5 at the last point - a factor of two above its own plateau, the right shape, and topping out just where the rubric says real stoppers top out. This is the one item where the chain agrees: is_stm 1. Two objects sit past the stop, and both are compact detached dots, each two points and 0.3 cm across, each drawn as an isolated marker clear of the amber body in c, d and e and each visible as a genuine isolated blob in all three f_meas planes (times 812 and 848 against the track end at 805), so they are measured charge and not fit artefacts. 93004 sits 17.6 cm out at cos_fwd +0.5 carrying 78784 e/cm and the chain independently calls it a capture gamma of 2.06 MeV; 94005 sits 11.0 cm out at cos_fwd -0.21, i.e. essentially sideways, so about 11 cm clear of the muon body line, carrying 15551 e/cm. Neither is an electron: the rubric is explicit that a 0.3 cm two-point speck across a gap of this size is not a 35 MeV electron, and there is no arm of any kind leaving the stop (n_stop_arms 0, no unfitted clusters). So both are gamma, the verdict stays STM_ONLY rather than STM_MICHEL - isolated capture gammas do not promote it - and michel_kind is detached dots.

A downgoing 68.5 cm cosmic: it enters 0.9 cm from the top y face at y 335 and the fit end sits 45.1 cm below it, 138 cm from the anode and 137 cm from the z wall, so the stop is interior. Upscaled, the last 15 cm are a textbook rise that follows the solid muon curve and peaks at the fit's own last point: 5.4-6.3e4 at s = 13-15, 7.1-7.6e4 at s = 12, 8.1-9.2e4 at s = 7-11, 9.5-1.02e5 at s = 5-8, 1.05-1.10e5 at s = 3-5, 1.25e5 at s = 1.5 and 1.32e5 at s = 0.7 - the maximum is the final point, there is no terminal dip and no forward high-charge tip, so neither the overshoot nor the undershoot applies and the pin stays put. (The chain does have a low trough of 0.5-2e4 around s = 18-32, which is the same periodic dQ/dx pathology that earns the plateau_off_mip rejection; it is 20 cm back and does not touch the stop.) Attached at the shared stop vertex 88004 is S88008, 18 points over 10.4 cm at an 88 deg kink, mean 5.6e4 e/cm, which the chain prices at 24.5 MeV over a 32.6 cm range. A muon sitting at a 1.32e5 Bragg peak has a few tens of MeV left and cannot continue at MIP, so that arm is a second particle, and 10 cm at MIP is exactly a ~25 MeV electron: Michel. The three azimuths show it directly - a blue arm leaving the star at right angles to the amber body and running to its own vertex square, with the muon's image-point halo ending at the star. The five remaining rows are 2-3 point specks at 42-47 cm scattered around the ring in unrelated directions: S379010, S380011 and S381012 sit on the muon body line at cos_fwd -0.89, -0.87 and -0.89, while S378009 and S382013 are forward (cos_fwd +0.57 and +0.94) but lie 114 and 150 deg away from the Michel arm, i.e. on the opposite side of the stop from the decay. None is on the Michel's side, so all five are delta / other and michel_kind is attached rather than both. Charge for the muon, the arm and the specks is real in U, V and W, and U and W are clear of dead bands at the stop.

column21: A 94.3 cm chain entering 0.2 cm from the z face and ending 46.0 cm from the nearest face, in_fv 1, and the chain already accepts it (is_stm 1). The Bragg is textbook and needs no argument: 4.5-5.5e4 plateau from s=50 to s=100, 6.5-7.5e4 at s=15-20, 7.5-9.0e4 at s=6-13, 9.4-9.8e4 at s=3-7, 1.07-1.11e5 at s=2 and 1.23-1.25e5 at the last two points, sitting on the solid muon curve the whole way up and topping out squarely in the 1.2-1.35e5 band. There is no terminal dip at all - the two highest points in the whole profile are the last two - so the pin stays put and neither failure mode is in play here. Past the stop a three-piece arm leaves at roughly a right angle to the muon: 79009 (11 points, 5.9 cm, 9.1e3 e/cm, d 0.0-3.41, cos_fwd -0.35) attached at the fit end, then 79011 (10 points, 5.5 cm, 4.1e4, d 2.41-7.28, cos_fwd -0.04) and 79012 (8 points, 4.0 cm, 2.3e4, d 7.28-10.62, cos_fwd -0.02), about 10.6 cm of charge at 0.17-0.76 of MIP. All three azimuths show it as a green-then-yellow chain of segments running away from the star through its own vertex squares, at a large angle to the muon and nowhere near hugging its body - cos_fwd near zero is perpendicular, not the -0.85-and-below that the delta rule wants - and it is inside 10 cm where the rubric says direction does not discriminate anyway. Attached, well clear of the body, sub-MIP: michel. A muon that has just put 1.25e5 into its last centimetre cannot carry on at a fifth to three quarters of MIP for another 10 cm. Then 180014, a 2-point 0.6 cm speck at 4.6e4 sitting 18.7-19.1 cm out at cos_fwd -0.26, which in the c and d azimuths lies beyond the far end of the arm and roughly along its direction, across a clear charge-free gap - isolated, compact, past the stop, inside 60 cm, clear of the body and on the Michel's own side, so gamma, and that gives kind both. I am overriding the chain's gamma body exclusion label on it, which the rubric explicitly permits when off-axis separation says otherwise. The last object, 179013, is a 2-point 0.3 cm speck 60.1 cm out at cos_fwd +0.19, flagged survey only and never offered to either stage; it is at the very edge of the 60 cm ring, its polar angle differs from the arm's by about 0.45 in cos_fwd, and in the c azimuth it sits on the opposite side of the stop from the arm, so I read it as an unrelated speck on the ring rather than part of this decay: delta / other. f_meas is clean - the stop is at U 3600, V 7370, W 12200 with the dead lines 30-40 channels off in U and V, and measured minus predicted is flat along the track.

column21: 281 cm, enters 1.4 cm from the anode face, stops 105 cm from the y wall. Bragg to 1.15e5 on the muon curve. A 9.8 cm arm at 5.1e4 e/cm leaves the stop forward (cos_fwd 0.61) with profile charge to -11 cm, and a further 0.5 cm piece the chain also calls Michel sits 16 cm out on the same side. Two dots at 40 and 51 cm, perpendicular and forward, clear of the body: gamma. 59005 lies 45-50 cm back ON the body line at 0.1 MIP: delta / other.

A short one: 39.2 cm of chain entering 0.1 cm from the x face at (340,261,257) and ending at (323,267,225), 17.2 cm back from that same face - close to the wall but inside it, and the profile removes any doubt. The plateau is 5.5-6.5e4 (segment 80005 averages 58003 over 31.7 cm from s=8 to s=37) and from about s=10 the chain climbs straight up the muon reference curve without a single reversal: 1.17e5 at s=10, 1.24-1.26e5 at s=6, 1.36e5 at s=5, 1.43e5 at s=2.5, 1.52e5 at s=1.5 and 1.62e5 at the last point, which is the only place in my chunk where the data actually reaches the reference curve. The last fitted segment 80004 averages 128070 e/cm over its 8.2 cm, 2.2 times the plateau, so the rise is in the segment table too. There is no terminal dip of any kind, so the pin stays where the fit put it and the overshoot question does not arise; the undershoot question does not arise either, since there is no forward piece past the tip at all. Past the stop the c, d and e azimuths show the amber band running into the star and nothing beyond it - no arm, no dot, no speck. The one other row, 200006, is an 11-point 5.8 cm stub at 14178 e/cm sitting 22-25 cm back at cos_fwd -0.99, and the d and e frames show it leaving the muon body sideways at that point, so it is body activity 22 cm up the track and tagged delta / other; it is nowhere near the stop and cannot bear on the kind. Michel_kind is none. The measured panels put the brightest charge in all three planes exactly at the stop end and no dead band within fifteen channels of it.

A 214.6 cm chain, 498.8 MeV by range with MCS agreeing at 467.7 (amb 0.09), entering 1.0 cm from the x face at the anode and ending 47.7 cm from the nearest (y) wall, in_fv 1; the chain accepts it as an STM. The dQ/dx panel is as clean as the best in this chunk: a 4.5-5.5e4 plateau from s=100 back to s=15 scattering about the flat solid muon curve, then a monotone climb that follows the curve all the way in - 6.5-7.2e4 at s=6-13, 8.9-9.3e4 at s=4-6, 1.03-1.09e5 at s=1.5-3, and 1.26e5 and 1.345e5 at the last two points, right in the 1.2-1.35e5 band and hugging the reference. There is no terminal dip whatever: the highest two points in the entire profile are the two nearest the origin, so neither failure mode applies and the pin stays exactly where the fit put it. This is the only item in my chunk with no non-chain object at all - the table has two rows and both are the muon's own fitted segments, 80002 spanning d 0-127.65 and 80005 spanning 127.65-201.16, both at cos_fwd about -1.0 as body segments must be. All three stop azimuths show the amber flow band running to the star and stopping there with nothing drawn beyond it: no arm, no dot, no speck, and no image-point halo past the end. The chain reports the same - n_stop_arms 0, n_dots 0, no capture gamma in the ring, 0 unfitted clusters - so there is nothing to weigh and the kind is none. f_meas is clean at the stop: it sits at U 2010, V 5805 and W 10120 with the nearest dead bands 40 to 90 channels away in every plane, and measured minus predicted is flat white along the whole track, so the Bragg is measured, not inferred.
